H07 Stage 1: audit and analysis plan

Absolute latitude, photoperiod, collection period, and possible exposure plateaus

Published

August 7, 2026

WarningHistorical Stage 1 gate and post-Stage 2 amendment

This document originally reconstructed the signed H07 contract, the submitted V0 model and GAM-derivative workflow, all stated deviations, candidate inputs, and the pre-fit support and identifiability problem. Its evaluated cells create formula objects and descriptive design summaries only; this Stage 1 document does not fit an inferential model.

The owner approved the original gate as H07-001 and later reopened its ceiling and support components after reviewing Stage 2. The post-result author revision is recorded as H07-002. Any computation-heavy bootstrap or simulation still requires a 50- or 100-replicate pilot, displayed runtime projection, and separate production approval.

1 How the revised ceiling question will be assessed

ImportantH07-002: revised derivative-defined plateau assessment

The owner has simplified the H07 question to whether a plateau-like photoperiod association is visible in the pooled observed data. For each of the nine metrics and each placement separately, the revised analysis:

  1. uses the already fitted site- and participant-adjusted photoperiod GAM;
  2. evaluates the first derivative of s(photoperiod_hours) at 100 equally spaced points from the exact metric-specific minimum to maximum recorded photoperiod;
  3. identifies a pointwise detected increase when the derivative’s 95% interval is wholly above zero;
  4. locates the first subsequent point whose interval contains zero; and
  5. classifies a derivative-defined plateau pattern only when every later point remains compatible with zero through the maximum recorded photoperiod.

The primary implementation uses central finite differences, forward/backward differences at the observed boundaries, a 0.01 h step, and unconditional covariance where available. The exact V0 forward, conditional, pointwise settings are a method sensitivity. The transition is reported as the grid bracket between the final detected-increase point and the first zero-compatible point.

The pooled-support, one-hour, and leave-one-site-out rules no longer determine eligibility. They remain diagnostics describing which sites and collection periods contribute to different curve regions and how site omission changes the fitted association.

This rule was chosen after inspection of the Stage 2 support results and is therefore a post-result descriptive definition. Its pointwise intervals have no curve-wide or cross-metric multiplicity control. An interval containing zero does not demonstrate practical equivalence, so the classification is not proof of an asymptote, a mechanistic ceiling, or a causal photoperiod effect. Site, latitude, photoperiod, and collection period limitations remain explicit but do not suppress the requested classification.

The revised implementation incorporates H11’s computational lesson without assuming that H11’s method transfers to H07. H07 has 655–816 primary near-eye participant-days and 743–902 complementary chest participant-days per metric, not H11’s large half-hourly Gaussian/AR(1) problem. The proposed primary engine is therefore exact mgcv::gam(method = "REML"). No primary step requires bam(discrete = FALSE). A checkpointed mgcv::bam(method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE) fit is only a computational fallback after a timed exact-fit attempt and must be checked against the exact GAM for fitted values, effective degrees of freedom, conditional AIC, supported predictions, and derivatives.

H11’s participant-cluster sandwich was validated for a Gaussian identity-link model after AR whitening. Its proposed family-aware extension to Tweedie is a new method, not an inherited result. H07 will use maintained mgcv inference as the primary conditional analysis and place any custom sandwich or participant-cluster refit bootstrap behind the H07-G7 method-validation pilot gate. Material residual dependence or failed identifiability prevents a confirmatory support claim until that gate is resolved.

2 Scope, terminology, and analytical boundary

H07 asks whether nine personal light-exposure metrics are associated with absolute latitude and civil photoperiod, whether the joint association is identifiable given the sites and collection periods, and whether any well-supported association can defensibly be called a plateau. The nine outcomes enter independently of H01 fitted results, p-values, or support classifications. H01 is used here only to reconstruct V0’s historical significance-dependent selection and to preserve the accepted metric and reporting terminology.

Near-eye measurement is primary. Chest measurement is complementary. Direct placement comparisons use the same participants and participant-days at both placements and retain separate models; placements are never pooled and no placement-equivalence claim is planned.

The predefined preparation sensitivity is the gap-timing-unaware dataset. It still passed the general 50%-per-hour and 80%-per-day coverage rules. The name means that the timing of the remaining missing observations was not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment; it does not mean that gaps, missingness, or coverage were ignored. For this one-time explanation, the primary could be interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset because its approved preparation uses the timing of remaining missing observations where relevant. From here onward it is called simply the primary dataset.

Reader-facing language uses melEDI, “period” rather than “bout,” and “bedside sleep-environment exposure” for the sleep metric. No temperature, weather, health outcome, clinical endpoint, unsupported predictor, causal effect, or physiological mechanism is introduced.

3 Registered H07 and decision provenance

3.1 Exact registered hypothesis

The signed preregistration states:

H7: There is a ceiling (nonlinear) effect of absolute latitude and photoperiod on level-, duration-, and exposure-history-based light metrics.

The signed generic model is Metric ~ te(Latitude, Photoperiod) + s(Site, bs="re") + s(Participant, bs="re"). The supporting developed analysis plan repeats the same tensor-product GAMM and expressly notes that identifiability may be a problem when latitude and photoperiod are both present. The registration also places chest first, uses near-eye as a robustness repeat, requires FDR control within hypothesis families, and uses a two-AIC-point rule for GAMM model comparison. The approved placement decision now makes near eye primary and chest complementary; that reversal is disclosed rather than hidden.

registered_h07_formula <- stats::as.formula(
  "Metric ~ te(Latitude, Photoperiod) + s(Site, bs = 're') + s(Participant, bs = 're')"
)
registered_h07_formula
Metric ~ te(Latitude, Photoperiod) + s(Site, bs = "re") + s(Participant, 
    bs = "re")

4 Exact V0 reconstruction

4.1 V0 formula objects and fitting rule

V0 filtered a global H01 result object by H1_phot_sig and metric category, then supplied the following exact formulas to mgcv::bam(). Both fits used discrete = TRUE, method = "fREML", and ten threads. Every response was log10(metric + 0.1), including durations with a point mass at zero.

v0_h07_formulas <- list(
  H7_full = stats::as.formula(
    "log_zero_inflated(metric) ~ s(photoperiod) + s(site, bs = 're') + s(Id, bs = 're')"
  ),
  H7_null = stats::as.formula(
    "log_zero_inflated(metric) ~ s(site, bs = 're') + s(Id, bs = 're')"
  )
)

enframe(v0_h07_formulas, name = "formula_id", value = "formula") |>
  mutate(formula = map_chr(formula, h07_formula_text))

V0 calculated dAIC = AIC(full) - AIC(null) and retained a model when dAIC < -2. This is a relative-support convention, not a significance test. For an mgcv::gam or mgcv::bam object, AIC() dispatches through logLik.gam() and uses the model’s conditional likelihood with effective degrees of freedom; it does not compare the stored fREML smoothing criterion. V0’s values are therefore potentially interpretable as conditional AIC evidence if the compared objects used identical response rows, family and link, weights, offset, likelihood implementation, and fitting engine, and if the smoothing-uncertainty-corrected edf2 provenance can be verified. Those historical object-level checks are not currently documented, so V0 conditional AIC is classified as provenance unverified, not inherently invalid. Its outcome-selection dependence and “significant” label remain invalid.

4.3 Exact V0 GAM-derivative method

The user correctly identified the derivative workflow as the substantive V0 method. The helper did not merely draw a smooth: it converted the final grid location with evidence of a positive derivative into the reported ceiling hour.

v0_derivative_call <- quote(
  deriv <- gratia::derivatives(model, select = "s(photoperiod)")
)
v0_boundary_rule <- quote(
  deriv_signif <- deriv |>
    dplyr::filter(.lower_ci > 0) |>
    dplyr::slice_tail(n = 1)
)

v0_derivative_call
deriv <- gratia::derivatives(model, select = "s(photoperiod)")
v0_boundary_rule
deriv_signif <- dplyr::slice_tail(dplyr::filter(deriv, .lower_ci > 
    0), n = 1)

With the pinned V0 gratia 0.11.2 defaults, this means a 100-point grid, first-order forward finite differences with eps = 1e-7, 95% pointwise confidence intervals, conditional smoothing-parameter uncertainty, and no simultaneous curve control. slice_tail() selects the final positive- derivative point even if positive regions are separated rather than sustained.

Interpretation of the V0 derivative algorithm
component v0_setting consequence
Derivative target s(photoperiod) only No latitude derivative or joint-surface plateau was evaluated
Grid n = 100 The labelled hour depends on a software-generated grid
Finite difference Forward; eps = 1e-7 No stability check across difference rule or step size
Uncertainty 95% pointwise confidence interval Repeated grid-point inspection is uncontrolled
Boundary Last row with lower CI > 0 Marks the end of detected increase, not equivalence to zero
Sustained interval None A later increase, decrease, reversal, or edge loss can be mislabelled as flattening
Support guard None The boundary can occur where only sparse sites or collection periods remain
Influence None No leave-one-site-out stability requirement
A non-significant derivative, an AIC threshold, and a visually flat smooth are each insufficient evidence of a ceiling.

V0 then described the last positive-derivative locations as ceilings around 14.7–16.4 h for level metrics and 16.6 h for time above 1,000 lx melEDI. The same near-eye and chest figure assembly duplicated daily mean and omitted M10. Every V0 threshold-hour and cross-placement ceiling claim is reopened.

5.2 Nine-metric response contract

All nine planned outcomes remain in scope even when a metric-specific model is non-estimable. Whole-day metrics describe the accepted hybrid measurement record, not uninterrupted 24-hour ocular exposure. The longest continuous period is an observed lower bound unless its boundaries are exactly identified. Corrected dose is available only when its relevance-support guard passes.

The first-to-last range does not imply uninterrupted sampling. Observed-date counts make sparse or separated collection periods visible.

Absolute latitude is one constant per site. Photoperiod is deterministically derived from site coordinates and local date. Photoperiod varies within some sites, but UCR and KNUST cover almost no within-site range in the near-eye data, whereas northern sites cover much wider but different calendar periods.

The site-plus-latitude design is rank deficient because latitude is exactly determined by site. A penalized random-site tensor may return a fit, but software convergence alone cannot separate site from latitude.
Photoperiod overlap across sites
Placement Sites All-site common lower All-site common upper All-site common width Pairwise overlap Median positive overlap
Near eye 9 16.41 h 12.35 h -4.06 h 28 / 36 1.05 h
Chest 8 16.41 h 12.35 h -4.06 h 21 / 28 1.00 h
A negative all-site width means that no photoperiod interval is observed at every site. Pairwise overlap does not create local replication of latitude because each latitude still belongs to one site.

The registered tensor therefore combines nine latitude stripes rather than a dense two-dimensional design. A fitted tensor can borrow smoothness across empty regions, but those interpolations are not observations. The high- photoperiod edge is especially vulnerable to northern-site and collection- period leverage.

7 Revised derivative estimand and the H07-002 decision

7.1 Association estimand

For metric (m), let μₘ(ℓ, p) be the population response-scale mean from the registered tensor at absolute latitude ℓ and photoperiod (p), with site and participant random effects set to zero. The primary registered association estimand is the joint contribution of the latitude–photoperiod tensor over the observed metric-specific support, conditional on the registered random effects. It is evaluated by a complete nine-metric model-evidence package:

  1. the maintained summary.gam() approximate whole-term test of the complete latitude–photoperiod tensor, assembled into the H07-F1-registered-association BH family;
  2. a prespecified approximate nested anova.gam() comparison of the tensor against its bilinear latitude-by-photoperiod subspace, assembled into the H07-F3-registered-nonlinear-shape BH family;
  3. conditional AIC differences for the full-versus-null and full-versus-bilinear candidate pairs as secondary relative-support evidence, never as p-values; and
  4. response-scale predicted surfaces and directional partial derivatives with 95% uncertainty only where the design-support rule permits them.

The tests are conditional, approximate GAM inference and not participant-cluster-robust by construction. They are released only if the registered tensor is identifiable and residual dependence is not materially inconsistent with the fitted participant random effect. The nested shape test also requires identical response rows, weights, offsets, family/link, and fitting method; a genuinely nested coefficient space; and greater effective degrees of freedom in the tensor model. Failure of any condition makes the affected p-value non-estimable rather than prompting a favourable alternative.

The exact REML tensor, null, and bilinear models are fitted on one locked metric-specific frame. AIC() is audited as mgcv conditional AIC, including whether edf2 is available, and the historical two-point convention is reported only as a descriptive relative-support label. The association test asks whether the tensor term is zero; the shape comparison asks whether the supported linear-predictor surface requires more than a bilinear form. Because every approved link is monotone, a constant linear predictor is also a constant response mean, but a bilinear linear predictor need not be bilinear after back-transformation. Practical estimates and derivatives are therefore reported on the response scale. None of these procedures establishes a plateau.

If the tensor is non-identifiable, a separately approved photoperiod-only smooth can estimate a narrower, adapted association conditional on site. It does not become the registered H07 result and cannot identify a latitude effect.

7.2 Derivative-defined plateau estimand

V0 evaluated the first derivative of the photoperiod smooth. H07-002 retains that direction and defines the requested visible plateau pattern for metric \(m\) and placement \(q\) on a 100-point metric-specific grid. Let \(d_{mq}(p)\) be the first derivative of the fitted s(photoperiod_hours) component on its model scale and let \([L_{mq}(p), U_{mq}(p)]\) be its pointwise 95% interval. A derivative-defined plateau pattern is present when:

  1. at one grid point, \(L_{mq}(p) > 0\), indicating a pointwise detected increase;
  2. the immediately following grid point has \(L_{mq}(p) \leq 0 \leq U_{mq}(p)\); and
  3. every later grid point through the exact maximum recorded photoperiod also has an interval containing zero.

The transition is interval-censored by the grid and is reported as the bracket between the final detected-increase point and the first zero-compatible point. A later pointwise detected increase or decrease makes the rule fail. No minimum tail length, site-overlap threshold, or leave-one-site-out stability requirement is imposed.

7.3 Equivalence and terminology boundary

No accepted source supplies a minimum practically important remaining slope for any of the nine heterogeneous metrics. H07-002 intentionally replaces the former equivalence estimand with a pointwise non-detection rule. Instrument resolution, model standard errors, a percentage chosen for convenience, and the two-AIC-point rule still cannot supply an equivalence margin.

Metric-specific equivalence-margin audit

The revised pointwise rule is not an equivalence test. An interval containing zero does not show that the remaining slope is scientifically negligible.
ImportantH07-002 interpretation

Stage 2 may report that a metric does or does not meet the requested derivative-defined plateau pattern. Because the decision is based on pointwise non-detection and was adopted after viewing Stage 2 output, it must remain labelled descriptive and post-result. It must not be translated into proof that the derivative is zero, a biological maximum has been reached, or the association generalizes independently of site and collection period.

7.4 Former sustained-support rule: diagnostic only

The original H07-001 design-support rule was defined from predictor geometry and outcome availability without examining metric values. It required:

  1. evaluate a 0.1 h photoperiod grid;
  2. a site contributes at a grid point only when the point lies within that metric/site’s 5th–95th photoperiod percentiles and the ±0.5 h local window contains at least five participants and 15 participant-days;
  3. a pooled point requires at least three sites, 20 participants, 60 participant-days, and no site contributing more than 50% of local days;
  4. the pooled rule must still pass after removal of every site; and
  5. a sustained interval requires at least 1.0 continuous h of eligible grid points.

H07-002 removes these thresholds as eligibility conditions. Their calculations are retained below to document cross-site overlap and upper-tail composition; they no longer censor the derivative grid or determine the revised plateau classification.

The primary near-eye design does not pass the former cross-site LOSO rule. Under H07-002 this shows that the upper curve cannot be interpreted as a site-replicated photoperiod response; it does not prevent asking whether the requested pattern is visible in the pooled fitted association.

8 Exact proposed model objects — no fits

8.1 Response construction and identifiers

Stage 2 will create response_value before fitting:

  • log10(value + 0.1) for daily mean, M10, L10, longest period, and corrected dose, fitted with a Gaussian family;
  • the natural non-negative value for the three Tweedie-log duration models, fitted with mgcv::tw(link = "log", a = 1.01, b = 1.99) so the compound-Poisson–gamma power is estimated inside fixed prespecified bounds; and
  • the natural-hour value for pre-sleep time, fitted with identity Gaussian.

The Tweedie contract is not justified by zero values and right skew alone. It assumes a compound occurrence–severity process for time above 1,000 lx melEDI, time above 250 lx melEDI during wake, and time below 1 lx melEDI during sleep. Stage 2 must report the fitted power, dispersion, distance from both power bounds, observed-versus-simulated zero frequency, and positive-tail calibration. A failure opens only the already accepted common-family decision gate; it cannot trigger a result-specific switch. If a two-part occurrence and positive-duration model is later judged scientifically necessary, its exact form must be approved before outcome-specific H07 results are inspected.

In the installed mgcv 1.9-4 environment, Stage 2 will attach mgcv before fitting tw() models and record that package state. The exact proposed family calls are visible below; this cell constructs calls but fits no model.

proposed_h07_family_calls <- list(
  gaussian_identity = quote(stats::gaussian(link = "identity")),
  tweedie_log_estimated_power = quote(
    mgcv::tw(link = "log", a = 1.01, b = 1.99)
  )
)

enframe(
  proposed_h07_family_calls,
  name = "family_id",
  value = "call"
) |>
  mutate(call = map_chr(call, h07_formula_text))

site_participant is interaction(site, Id, drop = TRUE) after the submitted site levels are fixed. Every model frame retains the original value, practical unit, transformation, local date, absolute latitude, photoperiod, site, participant, and exact row key.

8.2 Registered tensor and comparison formulas

The main tensor uses conservative fixed marginal basis dimensions k = c(4, 5). The expanded k = c(5, 8) formula is a mandatory basis- stability diagnostic, not an alternative selected by its p-value. The main tensor has a nominal marginal-basis product of 4 x 5 = 20 coefficients before constraints; the expanded diagnostic has 5 x 8 = 40. Their information demand is judged against only nine near-eye or eight chest latitude/site stripes and the metric-specific joint support, never against the participant-day row count alone. te() is retained because the complete joint surface is the estimand and no separate marginal smooths are included. The explicitly displayed tp margins are a pre-result basis decision; they will not be replaced after seeing results.

Every proposed primary H07 model uses mgcv::gam(method = "REML"). The null and bilinear formulas remain visible because they are the exact registered comparison structures and are fitted on the identical metric-specific rows for conditional AIC and the prespecified approximate nested comparison. The fixed-site version tests sensitivity to treating only nine site levels as a penalized random smooth; it cannot identify a latitude effect conditional on a saturated site factor and is interpreted only as a stability diagnostic. No numerical fit overrides the rank, concurvity, support-surface, or leave-one-site-out identifiability gates.

proposed_h07_registered_formulas <- list(
  registered_null = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ s(site, bs = 're') + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  ),
  registered_linear_surface = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ abs_latitude_deg * photoperiod_hours + s(site, bs = 're') + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  ),
  registered_tensor = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ te(abs_latitude_deg, photoperiod_hours, k = c(4, 5), bs = c('tp', 'tp')) + s(site, bs = 're') + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  ),
  registered_tensor_expanded_basis = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ te(abs_latitude_deg, photoperiod_hours, k = c(5, 8), bs = c('tp', 'tp')) + s(site, bs = 're') + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  ),
  registered_tensor_fixed_site = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ te(abs_latitude_deg, photoperiod_hours, k = c(4, 5), bs = c('tp', 'tp')) + site + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  )
)

enframe(
  proposed_h07_registered_formulas,
  name = "formula_id",
  value = "formula"
) |>
  mutate(formula = map_chr(formula, h07_formula_text))

8.3 Conditional photoperiod-only adaptation

These formulas are used only if the registered tensor fails the predeclared identifiability criteria and the author approves H07-G2. The adapted question is a site-adjusted photoperiod association over observed collection periods; it is not the registered joint latitude–photoperiod hypothesis.

proposed_h07_adapted_formulas <- list(
  adapted_photoperiod_linear = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ photoperiod_hours + s(site, bs = 're') + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  ),
  adapted_photoperiod_smooth = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ s(photoperiod_hours, k = 6, bs = 'tp') + s(site, bs = 're') + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  ),
  adapted_photoperiod_expanded_basis = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ s(photoperiod_hours, k = 10, bs = 'tp') + s(site, bs = 're') + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  ),
  adapted_photoperiod_fixed_site = stats::as.formula(
    "response_value ~ s(photoperiod_hours, k = 6, bs = 'tp') + site + s(site_participant, bs = 're')"
  )
)

enframe(
  proposed_h07_adapted_formulas,
  name = "formula_id",
  value = "formula"
) |>
  mutate(formula = map_chr(formula, h07_formula_text))

The registered null formula is reused as the adapted null. Primary, chest, paired/common, gap-timing-unaware, exact-period, observed-dose, and leave-one- site-out runs reuse these formula objects; only the predeclared rows or metric variant change.

Every primary model uses mgcv::gam(method = ‘REML’) on one locked metric-specific frame. Conditional AIC is relative-support evidence, not a test. Approximate p-values are withheld when identifiability, nesting, effective-df ordering, or residual-dependence conditions fail.

8.5 H11 computational lesson and H07 inference-validation gate

H11 established a project-local workaround after its large planned ML, discrete = FALSE fits ran for hours without a durable checkpoint. Its accepted test used an existing Gaussian identity-link fREML/discrete fit, AR-whitened raw-residual scores, participant CR1 covariance, Vp - Ve, and a finite-cluster fractional-rank F reference. Those identities were verified for that H11 model. They do not establish a general score, bread, covariance, or reference distribution for H07’s exact REML Gaussian-transformed and Tweedie-log models.

H07 therefore adopts only the portable lessons: checkpoint long fits; avoid an unnecessary bam(discrete = FALSE) branch; define the scientific contrast before results; and do not confuse failed computation with evidence. The primary H07 p-values use maintained mgcv interfaces under the explicit conditional-inference limitations above. The ordinary term test is not called cluster robust, and it is not interpreted when residual dependence, concurvity, or support failure invalidates that approximation.

If Stage 2 residual diagnostics show material within-participant dependence, the affected confirmatory support label is withheld. A participant-cluster repair can proceed only through a displayed 50- or 100-replicate pilot and a new author decision. The preferred pilot is a participant-cluster refit bootstrap that repeats the complete prespecified fit and test path. A custom sandwich pilot is permissible only if all of the following are demonstrated:

  1. the Gaussian identity-link implementation reproduces the accepted H11 score/bread result when AR whitening is absent or deliberately matched;
  2. Gaussian transformed-response and Tweedie-log scores and bread are checked against numerical likelihood derivatives and the model’s working weights;
  3. smoothing-parameter conditioning and any Vp - Ve addition are reported separately rather than assumed to be generally conservative;
  4. covariance eigenvalues, participant meat shares, contrast rank, finite- cluster denominator degrees of freedom, and representation invariance pass prespecified tolerances; and
  5. no production p-value relies on the unexported mgcv:::testStat() interface without a version-frozen validation against a maintained calculation.

Neither repair solves shared-site dependence, the nine/eight-site latitude–site confounding, or sparse joint support. Fixed-site and leave-one-site-out analyses remain mandatory limitations and influence checks.

The preregistered two-AIC-point rule and V0’s fREML dAIC values are retained as conditional-AIC relative-support evidence. New H07 conditional AIC is computed from the exact REML candidate fits only after all commensurability and edf2 checks pass. No ML likelihood-ratio branch or AIC-derived significance label is proposed.

Association and nonlinear shape retain their complete nine-member families. H07-002’s derivative pattern is a post-result descriptive classification based on unadjusted pointwise intervals, not a multiplicity-controlled test family.

All reader-facing p-values follow REPORT-008: leading zero, three decimal places, <0.001 below that threshold, and bold only when significant under the explicitly labelled raw or adjusted rule. Full precision remains in source CSVs.

9.2 Derivative and prediction contract

Stage 2 will recreate V0’s pointwise derivative rule exactly for historical comparison, including its 100-point default grid. Under H07-002, the revised derivative assessment will:

  • address metrics by ID and show each intended metric once;
  • evaluate gratia::derivatives() for s(photoperiod_hours) on the model/link scale at 100 equally spaced points from the exact metric-specific minimum to maximum recorded photoperiod;
  • use central differences with forward/backward boundary handling, a 0.01 h step, pointwise 95% intervals, and unconditional = TRUE where available;
  • classify the first positive-to-zero-compatible transition only when all later pointwise intervals contain zero through the recorded maximum;
  • report the transition as a grid bracket and report the remaining tail span;
  • retain the pooled-support and leave-one-site-out results as diagnostics, not masks or eligibility criteria;
  • reproduce the V0 forward, eps = 1e-7, conditional pointwise settings as a method sensitivity; and
  • call the result a derivative-defined plateau pattern, explicitly not an equivalence test, asymptote, mechanistic ceiling, or causal effect.

The requested rule uses analytic pointwise intervals and therefore requires no production simulation. A simultaneous-band sensitivity would require a new 100-replicate full-range pilot and separate production approval; it would test a stricter curve-wide question and would not turn non-detection into equivalence.

Primary near eye None Approved metric, tensor, support, and family contracts Primary registered analysis Any mandatory fit or identifiability failure
Complementary chest Placement and available site set Metric, formula, family, and diagnostic rules Complementary Material disagreement with near eye
Paired/common placement Restrict both placements to identical eight-site participant-days Separate fits and common effect scale Direct placement concordance Direction/magnitude incompatibility or invalid direct scale
Gap-timing-unaware dataset Prepared metric values and available days H07 implementation, support rule, and formulas Preparation sensitivity Material estimate, interval, support, influence, or conclusion change
Exact common preparation sample Restrict primary and gap-timing-unaware runs to identical keys Formula, response family, and predictors Value-versus-availability separation Scenario difference persists or reverses on common rows
Longest period exact-only Use only days whose observed lower and possible upper bounds coincide Formula and family Period-identifiability sensitivity Material curve, interval, or support change
Observed dose Replace corrected dose with observed dose on exact common rows Formula and family Correction-dependence sensitivity Material curve, interval, or support change
Expanded basis Use the displayed larger k Rows, family, random effects, and predictors Basis diagnostic Material curve/derivative change
Fixed-site representation Replace the penalized site smooth by fixed site Rows, participant effect, and predictor smooth Site-stability diagnostic Material shape change or exposed confounding
Leave one site out Remove one whole site per refit Response and approved formula structure Influence diagnostic Association/shape driven by one site or support collapses
Conditional photoperiod-only Remove latitude tensor and fit displayed site-adjusted photoperiod formulas Nine outcomes, rows, family, and multiplicity Adapted analysis only after H07-G2 Cannot be interpreted as registered H07 or as a ceiling
Temporal-precision repair Participant-cluster resampling or approved correlation sensitivity if required Estimand, formula, outcome, and support Conditional heavy-compute sensitivity Pilot indicates failure, instability, or prohibitive runtime
Sensitivities are interpreted for stability and are never searched for a preferred p-value. No season, temperature, weather, holiday, activity, or other unsupported predictor is added.

Collection period is handled as a design limitation and support display, not as an improvised categorical season covariate. Within a site, photoperiod is a deterministic function of date; across sites, calendar periods, routines, weather, holidays, and latitude differ. The fitted association is therefore observational and collection-period-specific. It is not a seasonal, climatic, behavioural, or causal effect.

11 Stage 2 implementation and V0-comparison plan

After approval, Stage 2 will:

  1. build an H07-owned model-row artifact from the four verified inputs, with exact keys, response transforms, site order, site_participant, metric variants, exclusions, and predictor support;
  2. attempt the registered tensor for every one of the nine metrics without consulting H01 support or H07 results;
  3. fit and checkpoint the exact full, null, and bilinear mgcv::gam(method = "REML") candidates on each locked metric frame; extract the maintained whole-term and prespecified nested approximate tests and audited conditional AIC; run no ML or bam(discrete = FALSE) branch;
  4. if an exact fit is not computationally practicable, display its timed attempt before invoking the bam(method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE) fallback as a provisional pilot; no fallback result is reportable until the same candidate on identical rows is benchmarked against an exact fit for fitted values, effective degrees of freedom, conditional AIC, supported predictions, and derivatives, or a new author gate explicitly revises that requirement;
  5. report exact fitted participants, participant-days, observations, and sites overall and by site, plus every 95% confidence interval and REPORT-008 p-value;
  6. interpret convergence, distributional, residual, physical-bound, temporal, identifiability, basis, support-surface, random-effect, and influence diagnostics rather than merely displaying them;
  7. run near-eye primary, chest complementary, paired/common placement, gap-timing-unaware, exact-common preparation, exact-period, observed-dose, basis, site-representation, and leave-one-site-out branches;
  8. classify an unidentifiable tensor as such and run the photoperiod-only adaptation only if H07-G2 is approved;
  9. reproduce V0’s H01-dependent candidate set, fREML AIC screen, default pointwise derivative grid, and last-positive rule, then apply H07-002’s positive-to-zero-compatible-through-the-end rule to the adapted models and separate changes caused by outcome selection, preparation, response family, tensor scope, comparison method, and derivative settings;
  10. recreate recognizable V0 near-eye and chest tables/figures while correcting the duplicated mean, missing M10, positional indexing, terminology, readability, and absent source data; and
  11. stop before any production participant-cluster bootstrap, custom sandwich release, or simultaneous-band simulation after displaying the required 50/100-replicate pilot and runtime estimate.

Under H07-002, Stage 2 reports a pointwise derivative-defined plateau pattern when the exact operational rule is met. It does not use a non-significant whole tensor, AIC threshold, or visual flattening for that classification and does not interpret the pattern as equivalence, an asymptote, or a causal or mechanistic ceiling.

12 Original Stage 1 decisions and post-Stage 2 amendment

The owner approved H07-G1 through H07-G16 as decision H07-001. After viewing the Stage 2 support output, the owner approved H07-002, which supersedes the ceiling disposition in H07-G1, the eligibility role of H07-G9, and the derivative prohibition in H07-G13. The remaining original decisions are retained below as the historical implementation record.

The original pre-Stage 2 decision package was:

  1. H07-G1 — ceiling claim (superseded by H07-002): accept the recommendation that no defensible metric-specific equivalence margin is available, disable H07-F2-plateau-equivalence, and prohibit ceiling/plateau claims for all nine outcomes. Any external margins must be supplied and approved before Stage 2 results are examined.
  2. H07-G2 — conditional adaptation: if the registered tensor is classified non-identifiable by the fixed diagnostic rule, approve a separately labelled photoperiod-only adapted analysis. It cannot replace or be called the registered H07 test.
  3. H07-G3 — outcome set: include all nine planned metrics independently of H01/H02 fitted results and retain reason-coded non-estimable family members.
  4. H07-G4 — estimands and maintained inference: approve the conditional approximate summary.gam() whole-tensor test, the prespecified approximate nested anova.gam() departure from the bilinear subspace, audited conditional AIC as secondary relative-support evidence, and practical-scale directional derivatives restricted to observed support. None is a plateau test, and failed identifiability or residual-dependence gates withhold a support claim.
  5. H07-G5 — response package: inherit the accepted H01/H05 metric-specific transforms, families, links, practical scales, and common-family failure rule; implement estimated-power mgcv::tw(link = "log", a = 1.01, b = 1.99) for the three Tweedie metrics with power/dispersion/boundary and joint zero/positive-tail diagnostics; reject V0’s one-log-Gaussian-model-for-all implementation.
  6. H07-G6 — formulas and basis: approve the exact displayed Wilkinson formulas, te() with tp margins, nominal 20/40 main/expanded tensor products, participant nested in site, fixed-site diagnostic, and exact gam(method = "REML") as the primary engine. Approve checkpointed bam(method = "fREML", discrete = TRUE) only as the documented fallback after a timed attempt; treat it as provisional until the same candidate and rows pass the exact-fit stability check.
  7. H07-G7 — H11-informed computation and repair gate: remove new ML and bam(discrete = FALSE) branches; do not assume H11’s Gaussian/AR-whitened CR1 construction transfers to transformed Gaussian or Tweedie H07 models; use maintained conditional GAM inference as primary and require a displayed 50/100-replicate method-validation pilot plus separate approval before any participant-cluster refit bootstrap or custom sandwich becomes reportable. Retain both V0 and new audited conditional AIC as relative-support evidence, never significance.
  8. H07-G8 — multiplicity: approve separate complete nine-member BH families for association and nonlinear shape in registered primary and separately named complementary/sensitivity runs; prohibit scalar adjustment and family shortening.
  9. H07-G9 — support rule (eligibility role superseded by H07-002): approve or revise the 0.1 h grid, central 90% site range, ±0.5 h window, 5-participant/15-day site threshold, 3-site/20-participant/60-day pooled threshold, 50% site-share cap, full leave-one-site-out requirement, and 1.0 h sustained interval before any outcome result is examined.
  10. H07-G10 — placement and samples: near-eye all-available is primary; chest all-available is complementary; direct placement comparison uses separate fits on exact paired/common participant-days; no pooling or equivalence language.
  11. H07-G11 — preparation and metric sensitivities: approve the gap-timing-unaware scenario-specific and exact-common comparisons, exact-period sensitivity, observed-dose sensitivity, and no result-based scenario selection.
  12. H07-G12 — collection period and predictors: treat collection date, site, latitude, and photoperiod confounding as a limitation/support audit; add no season category, temperature, weather, holiday, behavioural, or other unsupported predictor.
  13. H07-G13 — V0 derivatives (revised by H07-002): reproduce V0’s exact default pointwise derivative and last-positive rule only as a historical comparator; use central gratia::partial_derivatives() and gratia::response_derivatives() or full-predictor covariance-draw finite differences, supported grids, recorded uncertainty settings, and simultaneous bands for audited shape interpretation; never relabel end-of-detected-increase as a ceiling.
  14. H07-G14 — diagnostics and stop rules: approve the full diagnostic registry, non-identifiable/non-estimable dispositions, fixed basis/site sensitivities, participant influence, and leave-one-site-out checks.
  15. H07-G15 — temporal dependence and computation: interpret date-lag residual dependence within participant-specific contiguous-date series; no primary step may require bam(discrete = FALSE); material residual dependence withholds confirmatory support; if a resampling, custom covariance, or correlation sensitivity is required, run only a 50- or 100-replicate pilot and obtain separate production approval.
  16. H07-G16 — reporting language: report observational associations and collection-period limitations; make no causal, clinical, health-outcome, placement-equivalence, seasonal-mechanism, or unsupported ceiling claim.
CautionApproval status

H07-001 authorized Stage 2. H07-002 subsequently reopened and revised the plateau and support gates. The revised Stage 2 report must now be reviewed again before Stage 3 begins. No production bootstrap or simultaneous-band simulation is authorized by either decision.
